name: How much longer do custom homes take when there is a basement?

mainEntity.name: Does adding a basement significantly extend the schedule for a custom home build?
mainEntity.text: Does adding a basement significantly extend the schedule for a custom home build?

acceptedAnswer.text: A basement usually adds meaningful time to a custom home schedule because the work below grade is more complicated than a simple slab or crawlspace foundation. Excavation may require shoring, haul-off, soils coordination, and additional waterproofing details. If the site has a slope or poor soil conditions, the basement can trigger more engineering and inspection requirements. In Los Angeles, basements often affect permitting and construction sequencing because the team must resolve structural and drainage issues before framing can begin. The time impact depends on size, depth, site access, and whether the basement is fully habitable or partially mechanical space. Homeowners should expect more preconstruction design effort and more schedule risk than they would with a shallow foundation. Basements can add value, but they should be planned as a major structural component rather than an upgrade that is easy to insert later.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, a basement usually adds time because excavation, shoring, waterproofing, structural design, and inspections are more complex. Basement construction also increases the chance of soil and drainage issues that must be resolved before the project can continue. On tight sites, the extra work can be substantial.
